title: Documentation + CS enablement for Dedicated autoscaling bounds & predictive mode
creator: Talia Benson
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Goal
Produce customer-facing documentation and Customer Success / Support enablement materials for Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) + predictive mode.

This ticket is required for pilot expansion + GA. It should result in:
1) clear semantics (what is enforced, precedence, failure modes)
2) actionable configuration guidance (how to choose min/max + cooldowns)
3) troubleshooting steps tied to dashboards/alerts/runbooks
4) support macros / internal FAQ for faster consistent responses

Background
Enterprise Dedicated customers are requesting explicit guardrails:
- hard max capacity bounds to prevent unexpected spend
- min baseline capacity to protect SLOs
- optional predictive scaling for known traffic ramps

We’ve implemented the core feature work behind feature flags. Support/CS needs consistent guidance and “what to do when” playbooks, especially for:
- max bound saturation causing queueing
- unmet min bound during region capacity shortage
- predictive mode oscillation / staleness / timezone confusion

Scope / Deliverables
A) Customer documentation updates (redwood-docs)
- Update Dedicated autoscaling docs to include:
  - Definitions: min_replicas, max_replicas, cooldowns, predictive_mode
  - Enforcement semantics: desired vs bounded desired; never exceed max; never drop below min (except if region shortage prevents provisioning)
  - Precedence: customer bounds override platform defaults; reactive signals override prediction when prediction is wrong, still clamped to bounds
  - Migration notes: existing deployments unchanged until enabled (feature flag + policy enabled)
  - How to enable (Console + API + Terraform when available)
  - Recommended starting ranges (by workload pattern) + warnings for high mins
- Add a troubleshooting section with “symptom → diagnosis → mitigation”:
  - Symptom: sustained queue depth + p95 latency; dashboard shows bounded_desired == max
    - Mitigation: raise max (contract permitting), enable burst pool (if available), reduce token limits / concurrency, enable fallback routing (if configured)
  - Symptom: predictive enabled but no early scale-up
    - Check forecast freshness, timezone alignment, and feature flag; verify prediction confidence panel
  - Symptom: oscillation / jitter
    - Check cooldown settings; verify predictor staleness; confirm anti-oscillation guardrails enabled; consider disabling predictive temporarily
  - Symptom: min bound not met
    - Explain region shortage behavior + degraded state; what Redwood does (retry/backoff) and what customer can do (temporary lower min, alternate region if contract permits)

B) Support macros (Zendesk/Jira responses) + internal FAQ
- Provide short templated responses for top ticket types:
  1) “Autoscaling exceeds budget cap” → explain max bound and how to set it; how to interpret bound-hit metrics
  2) “Queueing during daily ramp” → explain predictive mode; lead time expectations; how to validate forecasts and success criteria
  3) “How to set bounds for SLA” → guidance to pick min based on steady-state throughput + headroom; max based on budget + peak; suggest staged tuning
  4) “Min not met during shortage” → explain degraded state; comms; how to set expectations / escalation path
- Internal FAQ should cover:
  - What we mean by “hard” vs “recommended” bounds
  - What to check first in dashboards
  - When to page SRE vs route to Dedicated support vs route to infra capacity planning

C) CS enablement materials
- 1-page “talk track” for CSMs/TAMs:
  - What the feature solves
  - How to position in QBRs
  - Common pitfalls
  - Suggested rollout plan (pilot → canary → GA)
- Checklist for pilot onboarding:
  - Confirm customer timezone + ramp schedule
  - Confirm initial min/max + cooldowns
  - Confirm alerts + dashboard access
  - Confirm escalation channel + runbook link

D) Cross-linking + canonical sources
- Ensure docs link to:
  - Confluence PRD and ADR for semantics (internal)
  - SRE troubleshooting runbook (internal)
  - Observability dashboard spec (internal)
  - Known issues for predictive mode (internal)
- Ensure there is one “canonical” semantics source for Support (likely ADR + customer docs).

- Runbook: /eng-infra/runbooks/dedicated-autoscaler-troubleshooting-runbook
- Dashboard spec: /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/autoscaling-bounds-observability-dashboard-spec

- Docs PR (target): sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2442-dedicated-autoscaling-bounds-customer-docs.json

Acceptance Criteria
- Customer docs merged and published:
  - Includes min/max/predictive semantics and troubleshooting section
  - Includes clear warnings around high min bounds + shortage behavior
- Support macros delivered to Support lead and stored in the support playbook location
- CS 1-pager + pilot onboarding checklist delivered to CS lead and shared in the pilot Slack channel
- SRE and Product reviewers approve wording around safety invariants, degraded behavior, and when to page/escalate

Out of Scope
- Contract language templates (handled by Sales/Legal)
- Deep forecasting methodology documentation (we should describe operational behavior, not model internals)

Risks / Notes
- We must be careful about promises around min bound: in shortage scenarios we may not be able to provision immediately. Docs must describe degraded state and expected alerting, and avoid implying absolute guarantee beyond contract terms.
- Avoid suggesting high-cardinality metrics labels in customer docs; keep dashboards guidance aligned with Observability spec.

Next Steps
1) Draft troubleshooting matrix + support macros (Diego + Dev)
2) Send for SRE review (Rafael) and Product review (Lauren)
3) Land docs PR + publish
4) Announce in #support and #customer-success with links and “what changed” summary
